title: PXAPI sampling manifest v1
description: Which population of one site's pages an Analysis Run actually set out to analyse, and why — bound to the exact inventory it was selected from and to the exact policy version that selected it. It exists so that every later measurement, evidence item and finding can be traced back to the page population it was drawn from, rather than to an unrecorded choice. Selection is Pixelkiez methodology: no member of this contract names, admits or defers to a crawl provider, and nothing here lets a provider decide which pages become diagnosis-relevant. It is not a score authority and not an assessment: mode, selection_complete, every selection reason and every exclusion reason are statements about this analysis, and none of them may be read as a judgement of the website. selection_complete is mandatory and neutral in both values: false means the selection was bounded or otherwise incomplete, never that the site is deficient. The census-to-sampling threshold is deliberately absent — STRATIFIED_SAMPLE exists in the vocabulary so that a manifest can say which method was used, and its presence in this contract is not a claim that a benchmark-authorised sample can currently be produced.

schema_version.description: Required. Always 1.0.0 for this contract. Each contract is versioned in its own right; this value is not a version of the contract set as a whole.

run_id.description: Required. The Analysis Run this manifest belongs to. It is the only link to the run's state document, and it carries no claim about that run's outcome.

sampling_manifest_id.description: Required. This manifest's own stable identity, so that a later acquisition or diagnosis can reference the manifest it worked from rather than restating it.

generated_at.description: Required. When this manifest was produced. A selection with no instant cannot be compared with a later selection over the same site.

inventory_ref.description: Required. The inventory_id of the site inventory this selection was drawn from. It names which inventory; inventory_output_digest is what pins which version of it.

inventory_output_digest.description: Required. The exact site-inventory output_digest this selection was made against, so a manifest can never be read as a selection over a population it did not see. It is required rather than optional because this manifest's own input_digest is computed over it: an absent binding would leave the input digest covering a population nobody can identify. It is a binding to the inventory's semantics and never a replacement for this manifest's own input_digest.

policy_id.description: Required. A stable machine-readable identifier for the selection policy that produced this manifest. The vocabulary is deliberately open: this contract fixes the token's lexical shape and never the set of policies, so a policy a later slice introduces validates here without a schema change.

policy_version.description: Required. The version of the selection policy. Two manifests over the same inventory are comparable only when the policy and this version agree, so the version travels with the manifest rather than being assumed. A policy whose selection rule changes is a new version of that policy.

budgets.description: Optional. The decision-relevant bounds the policy was run under, present if and only if at least one was declared. Every member is a whole number: a bound expressed as a floating-point value could not be digested deterministically, so none is representable here. Absent means no bound was declared for this selection, which says nothing about the site.

max_selected_pages.description: Optional. The declared ceiling on how many pages this selection may name. Reaching it is a bound of this analysis, recorded as an exclusion reason and as selection_complete false, never as a property of the site.

max_candidates_considered.description: Optional. The declared ceiling on how many inventory candidates the policy examined. Reaching it means the selection was bounded, which is why selection_complete exists.

mode.description: Required. Which selection method produced this manifest. The vocabulary is closed at two values: CENSUS means every eligible candidate of the bound inventory was selected, and STRATIFIED_SAMPLE means a deterministic policy drew a subset across strata. The threshold at which a population moves from one to the other is deliberately not stated by this contract and is not derivable from it: it remains an open, benchmark-dependent policy decision, and this contract carries no number that could be mistaken for it.

selection_complete.description: Required. Whether the policy ran to its own defined end over the bound inventory. It is mandatory rather than optional because a selection read without this fact is the most likely way this contract gets misused: a partial selection would otherwise look like a complete one. Both values are neutral. false means the selection was bounded or otherwise incomplete — a budget was reached, or the policy stopped early — and it is a statement about this analysis; it never means the site is small, thin, deficient or incompletely built, and nothing downstream may treat it as a penalty.

items.description: One selected page: its canonical identity, its position in the deterministic selection order, why the policy selected it, and the stratum it was counted under if any.

url_key.description: Required. The canonical identity of the selected candidate, as carried by the bound inventory. It is an identity and not a fetch instruction: acquiring it is a later slice's decision and this manifest proves no fetch.

selection_rank.description: Required. This selection's position in the policy's deterministic order, counting from one. The rank and not the array position is the authority on order, so re-serialising the document in a different array order cannot change what the manifest means or what its output digest is. Ranks are dense and ascending across the selections of one manifest.

selection_reason.description: Required. Why the policy selected this candidate.

stratum.description: Optional. The stratum this selection was counted under, as a stable open token: this contract fixes the token's lexical shape and deliberately not the stratum taxonomy, which is versioned methodology work rather than a set invented here. Absent means the selection was not counted under a stratum, which says nothing about the page.

selections.description: Required. The selected pages, in the policy's deterministic order. At least one is required, for the same reason the inventory refuses an empty candidate list: a manifest selecting nothing would read as a successful analysis of no pages, when what happened is that selection produced nothing — a neutral technical outcome that belongs to the run rather than to this document. A selection is deliberately not a fetch result and carries no transport outcome, no artifact and no measurement.

items.description: How many inventory candidates were not selected, per technical reason. It is a bounded summary and deliberately not a list of URLs.

reason.description: Required. The technical reason these candidates were not selected.

candidate_count.description: Required. How many candidates this reason accounts for. It is at least one, because a reason that excluded nothing is not an exclusion and would only add noise to the summary.

exclusions.description: Required. A per-reason count of the inventory candidates this selection did not take, so a reader can see the shape of what was left out without the manifest carrying a page list. It is a summary by design: an arbitrary URL string is deliberately not persisted here merely so that a digest can be recomputed, and a candidate that was not selected is not thereby a defect of the website. An empty list means nothing was left out — it never means the site has no other pages. Each reason appears at most once; the order of this list carries no meaning, and the output digest reads it under a canonical ordering.

input_digest.description: Required. The canonical digest of everything this selection was decided from — the bound inventory reference and its output digest, the policy identity and version, and the declared budgets — computed over a deterministic UTF-8 JSON rendering with sorted keys, no floating-point members and a canonical ordering of every order-independent collection. Envelope identities and timestamps, and the two digest members themselves, do not participate. Two manifests with the same input digest were decided from the same inputs; whether they selected the same pages is what output_digest says.

output_digest.description: Required. The canonical digest of this manifest's stable selection semantics — mode, selection_complete, the selections in rank order, and the exclusion summary under a canonical ordering — computed over the same deterministic canonical JSON. Envelope identities and timestamps, and the two digest members themselves, do not participate, so re-emitting the same selection under a new manifest id at a new instant leaves this value unchanged. Selection order is semantic here and is read from the ranks, which is why reordering the array cannot change it while reordering the ranks can. There is deliberately no third content_digest: input and output are the whole digest topology.

selection_reason.description: Why a deterministic selection policy took one candidate. The vocabulary is closed, because a reason is what keeps a selection attributable to the method rather than to an unrecorded judgement, and an open token could carry a reason that describes the page instead of the policy. SEED means the candidate is the canonical target seed, which every selection takes. CENSUS means the mode is CENSUS and the candidate was eligible in the bound inventory. STRATUM_QUOTA means a deterministic sampling policy drew it to fill a stratum's quota. None of the three ranks a page above another, and none is a relevance, quality or priority statement.

exclusion_reason.description: Why inventory candidates were not selected. The vocabulary is closed for the same reason the selection reasons are, and every token names this analysis: NOT_SELECTED_BY_POLICY means the deterministic policy did not draw them; SELECTION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED means a declared bound of ours was reached first; INELIGIBLE_IN_INVENTORY means the inventory had already recorded a technical exclusion for them. Not being selected is a fact about this run's method and budgets, never a defect of the pages concerned.
